sentences.text: Pyroraptor was a small, bird-like dromaeosaurid covered in feathers, similar to its relatives Microraptor and Sinornithosaurus.
Its known teeth were flattened and curved backwards, featuring finer serrations on the rear margins than the front.
This predator possessed a sickle claw measuring 6.5 centimeters on the second toe of each foot.
The genus name means "fire thief" because the fossils were discovered following a 1992 forest fire.
The specific name "olympius" honors Mont Olympe, the mountain near where the remains were found.
The holotype specimen, the single bone the species is based on, consists only of the left foot's second claw.
A single specimen was discovered in 1992 in Provence, southern France, at the locality of La Boucharde in the Arc Basin.
The species was named Pyroraptor olympius by paleontologists Ronan Allain and Philippe Taquet in 2000.
Pyroraptor possessed long arms with sharp claws used to grip its prey.
It was a bipedal hunter with a small and slender body shape that indicates it was a fast animal.
Researchers suggest Pyroraptor's enlarged claws may have been used as weapons or for climbing.
Pyroraptor is classified within the family Dromaeosauridae and belongs to the subfamily Dromaeosaurinae.
It is considered a "wildcard taxon" that creates instability in phylogenetic analyses unless it is removed.
A 2019 study suggested Pyroraptor might be an unenlagiine, but a 2021 study ruled this out because its teeth differ significantly from those of unenlagiines.

Pyroraptor lived during the Late Cretaceous, approximately 70 million years ago in the Maastrichtian stage, with a time range estimated from the Campanian to the Maastrichtian, between 83.6 and 66 million years ago.

Fossils are known from the Argiles et Grès à Reptiles Formation in what is now southern France, where the animal lived on the island landmass of Ibero-Armorica formed from modern-day southern France and northern Spain in the Tethys Ocean.
It is debated whether the known Pyroraptor remains belong to a single individual due to their disarticulated nature.
A 2012 study argues that many traits considered unique to Pyroraptor are actually widespread among dromaeosaurids or caused by preservation deformation.
The possibility that Pyroraptor and Variraptor are the same species is raised, but it cannot yet be tested due to a lack of overlapping fossil material.
A 2022 study noted that Pyroraptor's foot morphology resembles unenlagiines more than eudromaeosaurs, supporting the idea that European raptors were related to Southern Hemisphere forms.
